deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. The page is written upside down relative to the rest of the notebook, which suggests it was entered from the other end of the book. It is a tabular shopping or inventory memorandum for textiles, headed 'Dimitty' (dimity, a light, sheer cotton fabric, usually with raised stripes or checks).

Each line has four parts:
1. A piece or pattern number (No. 3, 73, 6, 7, 8, 9, 1, 3, 2, 10, 1, 3, 4, and a dash).
2. A length, most plausibly in ells: 10 3/4, 4 3/4, 26 3/4, 17 3/4, 4, 13, 19, 12, 12, 12, 12, 11 1/2, 37 1/2, 11 1/2. The first entry carries an 'Ell'-like abbreviation.
3. A fabric description, mostly 'do' (ditto). Others are 'Mouslinett' (mousseline / muslinet), a word read as 'Pagne' (uncertain), 'Jacc.' (possibly jacquard or jaconet), 'Spot' (spotted muslin, with an earlier spelling struck through and rewritten), and 'Jacon. Mouslin' (jaconet muslin).
4. A right-hand number between about 12 and 19, presumably a unit price (e.g. groschen per ell) or a width.

The dotted leaders joining description to the final number are typical of a price list.

No computation is carried out on the page. Gauss gives no total, product or derivation; it is a household or commercial note. The neighbouring pages are also domestic notes: pendulum lengths, clock screw calibrations, family birth dates and children's heights on the previous page, and wallpaper and room measurements on the next.

The only implicit arithmetic one could form (mine, not Gauss's) is the total length: 10.75+4.75+26.75+17.75+4+13+19+12+12+12+12+11.5+37.5+11.5 = 204.5, if the readings are correct.
errors: None identifiable: the page contains a list, not a derivation. Several readings of the fractions and fabric names are uncertain from the image.

transcription_corrections: The page is written upside down (rotated 180°) relative to the folio numbering '105'.
'Dimitty' = dimity (cotton fabric); the whole page is a textile list, not mathematics.
The struck-through word in line 'No. 10' is an earlier spelling of 'Spot', rewritten as 'Spot' (spotted muslin).
'Jacon. Mouslin' in the last line is best read as jaconet muslin. 'Jacc.' in line 'No. 2' may likewise be jaconet or jacquard; this is uncertain.
Final column values (e.g. 12¾ vs 12½ in the first line, 13½ in the second) are uncertain; the fraction glyphs are ambiguous in the image.
'm Pagne' in line 6 is uncertain; it may be a fabric name (e.g. 'Pique'), unverified.
